what: Proposed Step 18 skips restore whenever Python has written finalize-state.sh, even if ship-pr-state.sh was changed later
scenario_or_breakage: After Python exits transient or needs-user and the selector or Step 18a marks STALL_TRACKING=true in ship-pr-state.sh, finalize-state.sh can still say false; teardown then treats the run as non-stalled and may clean up artifacts
suggested_fix: Restore when finalize-state.sh is missing or ship-pr-state.sh has terminal fields that require teardown, at minimum STALL_TRACKING=true, BAIL_NEEDS_USER_INPUT=true, or changed STALL_STEP; skip only when finalize-state is known current

what: Terminal Python writes preserve seeded bash state keys but do not set bash-compatible terminal keys for the actual outcome
scenario_or_breakage: Default Python returns STALLED or NEEDS_USER_INPUT; final report and stall recovery consume EXIT_CODE, BAIL_REASON, BAIL_NEEDS_USER_INPUT, and related state, so defaults can produce wrong outcome text or EXIT_CODE=0 in recovery reports
suggested_fix: Extend the terminal writer to overlay outcome-derived EXIT_CODE, STALL_TRACKING, STALL_STEP, BAIL_REASON, BAIL_NEEDS_USER_INPUT, FAILED_RUN_ID, and BAIL_FAILURE_DETAIL_LOG where available; ensure final-bail-reason remains restore-compatible
